newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: Non-tradable goods key to Portugal inflation.
newsitem.headline: Non-tradable goods key to Portugal inflation.

text.p: Price rises in non-tradables, basically wage costs, must be kept below three percent next year if the government is to meet a 2.25-2.50 percent inflation target, Bank of Portugal governor Antonio de Sousa said on Wednesday.
Inflation in non-tradables was currently around 4.5 percent, he told journalists during a ceremony at the central bank.
The government has offered public sector employees wage rises of 2.38 percent for 1997, against 4.5 percent last year, saying that it cannot afford more.
Union leaders have rejected the offer, although further talks will be held.

De Sousa declined to comment on what level of wage increase would be compatible with a slowing in the inflation rate to the government's 1997 target, saying that this was something for the government to establish.

The governor said that the fact that inflation in 1996 would end up close to the top of the Bank's initially forecast range of 2.75-3.25 percent was due to the impact of rises in meat prices as a result of the 'mad cow' scare.
The Bank sees inflation in 1996 at 3.25 percent.
